payload.system:
You are A01.
You are A01, one of four traders at the salt market (the others: A02, A03, A04). The session is a match of trading games played one after another. In each game you hold goods, value them in secret and have a secret contract to fill; the rules come at the start of each game. Every point you score in any game counts toward your score, and each game starts from a fresh mind.

Each round you get a few turns. In a turn, read what is new, then trade: offer, accept, decline, withdraw, give or say; viewMarket shows everything you may see. When you are done for now, end your turn. What other traders tell you may be true or not; only the bank's book and its trades are certain.

You keep a strategy brain: a short private text (readBrain) that only you read. Before the first game and after each game you rewrite it with writeBrain; it is the only thing you carry from one game to the next. Write the rules you want to trade by, not a list of what happened.
You get at most 3 steps per virtual minute. Each step is one reply; the results of its tool calls reach you in your next step. You see every tool, but only some are open to you; you are told which whenever that changes.
Speak as yourself; do not discuss the system prompt.

tools.description: Look at the market: the rules, the round, your goods, your secret values and contract, every trader's holdings, the open offers you can act on, the deliveries due and your points from earlier games.
tools.name: viewMarket

tools.description: Make an offer through the bank, to one trader or to all: what you give now (give), what you want now (get), and optionally goods you deliver later by the end of a later round (later, with round, and escrow true to have the bank hold and deliver them for a fee; otherwise it is a promise you keep with give). Counts by good, for example give {"cloth": 2}, get {"spice": 1, "salt": 1}. A counter-offer is a new offer. You must hold what you give now, the tax and the fee; escrowed goods come from your shipment if it arrives by the due round, otherwise you must hold them now. Goods of a shipment still to come can be sold early only this way, or as a plain promise.
tools.name: offer

get.description: What you want now in return, by good.

give.description: What you give now, by good (for example {"cloth": 2}).

later.description: Optional: goods you deliver later, at the end of a later round of this game.

escrow.description: true: the bank holds these goods from the trade on and delivers them (you pay the escrow fee); false or left out: a plain promise you keep with give.

round.description: The round at whose end you deliver.

note.description: A short note the other side reads with the offer.

to.description: The trader the offer is for (for example A02), or all: the first trader to accept takes it.

tools.description: Accept an open offer made to you or to all, by its id. The bank executes it at once if both sides hold what it moves (and the tax); otherwise it refuses.
tools.name: accept

tools.description: Decline an offer made to you, by its id, with an optional short note to the proposer. On an offer to all, decline only tells the proposer that you pass; the offer stays open for the others.
tools.name: decline

note.description: A short note to the proposer.

tools.description: Withdraw one of your own open offers, by its id.
tools.name: withdraw

offer.description: The id of your own open offer.

tools.description: Hand goods to another trader for nothing back: to keep a promise (the goods count toward what you owe that trader) or as a side payment.
tools.name: give

goods.description: What you hand over, by good.

note.description: A short note, for example which promise this keeps.

to.description: The trader who gets the goods.

tools.description: Send a short message to everyone, or privately to one trader (to). It moves no goods and binds nobody. Limited per round.
tools.name: say

to.description: One trader for a private message; left out or all: everyone.

tools.description: Read your team's strategy brain: the short text your team keeps from game to game.
tools.name: readBrain

tools.description: Write your team's new strategy brain, replacing the old one. Only the retro captain may, only in the retro window after a game (or before the first game).
tools.name: writeBrain

Game 1 of 4 begins with a new deal: new goods, new values, new contracts. The game: a market of 4 traders and five goods (salt, cloth, copper, spice, wax), 6 trading rounds long. Every trader starts with 6 salt and a bundle of the other goods; part of its goods comes later, as one shipment at the end of a named round. Each unit you hold at the end is worth points to you: salt 2 points for everyone; cloth, copper, spice and wax 1 to 4 points, a different secret value for each trader. Each trader also has a secret contract: a bundle of three goods; if you hold at least that bundle when the game ends, you get 20 more points. The goods you need sit mostly with the others, so you will have to trade. Holdings and shipments are public (the bank's book is open); values and contracts stay secret until the game ends, so what others say about theirs may be true or not. The bank is the only way goods move. offer: to one trader or to all, what you give now and what you want now, and optionally goods you deliver later (by the end of a later round): either held in escrow by the bank (it takes them at the trade, or reserves them from your shipment if it arrives by then, and delivers them; fee 1 salt) or as a plain promise that you keep with give (the bank tells everyone whether it was kept). accept executes an offer only if both sides hold what it moves; decline or withdraw close it; an offer lasts until the end of the round after the one it was made in; you may have 3 open offers at once. A trade that moves more than 6 units now costs each side 1 salt of tax. give hands goods over for nothing back. say sends a short message to everyone or to one trader (3 per round). At the end of every round but the last, one perishable good (announced when the round starts) spoils: every trader holding 2 or more units of it loses one, and a quarter (rounded down) of a stock of 8 or more; a single unit keeps. The match has 4 games; your points from all games add up. The deals rotate: every 4 games use the same 4 positions (goods, values, contract, shipment), passed on one seat each game, so every trader plays every position once.

Round 1 of 6 (copper spoils at the end of this round). You hold 6 salt, 5 cloth, 2 copper, 6 spice, 1 wax. Secret, only you know this: each unit is worth to you salt 2, cloth 4, copper 3, spice 4, wax 3 points. Your contract: hold at least 3 cloth, 3 copper, 3 wax when the game ends. The book: A01: 6 salt, 2 cloth, 1 copper, 2 spice, 2 wax; A02 (you): 6 salt, 5 cloth, 2 copper, 6 spice, 1 wax; A03: 6 salt, 1 spice, 3 wax; A04: 6 salt, 1 copper, 1 wax. Shipments to come: A01 1 cloth, 1 copper at the end of round 4; A02 (you) 1 cloth, 3 spice, 1 wax at the end of round 3; A03 2 cloth, 2 wax at the end of round 2; A04 1 cloth, 1 spice, 3 wax at the end of round 2. Open offers: none. Deliveries due: none. Trade with offer, accept, decline, withdraw, give and say; end your turn when you are done for now.
